clinician.trajectory_summary: A 28-year-old male presented with a 2-month history of nonproductive progressive cough and left flank pain. Physical examination revealed abdominal distention with a large left upper quadrant mass and left flank tenderness. Initial staging workup included chest CT (E001) showing a heterogeneously enhancing left retroperitoneal mass, and MRI (E002) which characterized a 155×140×150 mm left suprarenal mass with lobulated margins, central cystic changes, diffusion restriction, and heterogeneous enhancement, along with metastatic left para-aortic lymphadenopathy and multiple metastatic nodules in bilateral lung lower lobes and liver (explaining the cough). Tissue biopsy was performed, with histology (E004) demonstrating small round cells. Immunohistochemistry (E005) showed tumor cells negative for LCA, WT-1, DESMIN, Myogenin, phox-B2, CD99, SOX10, Chromogranin, and GATA3, but positive for CK, FLI-1, and Synaptophysin. The pathology report concluded the findings were compatible with renal PNET/Ewing sarcoma.
